items.period: Shang oracle-bone script style; the redraw is not a securely dated specimen.
items.caption: This modern redraw in Shang oracle-bone script style shows 大 as a frontal human figure, with a long upright body, slanting side strokes, and separated legs. Sources agree on the human-figure interpretation but differ on how to read the pose.
items.alt: Black glyph with a long upright center, two slanting side strokes, and separated legs.
items.selection_reason: This early-style form illustrates the whole-graph human-figure analysis. Its shape does not resolve the differing interpretations of the pose.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page.

items.tradition: Seal script as represented in Shuowen-style reference forms
items.caption: This modern redraw in Shuowen seal-script style retains an upright center, outward-sloping arms, and two long legs. It offers a broad comparison with the earlier-style form, but does not show a precise sequence of graphic changes.
items.alt: Black seal-style glyph with a central upright, sloping arms, and two long legs.
items.selection_reason: The later script-style comparison helps show the broad continuity of the human-like outline; the evidence does not establish detailed changes between forms.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: These redrawings represent script styles rather than photographs of ancient objects. The human-figure interpretation is shared, but accounts differ on the pose; the shapes alone cannot establish the figure’s original meaning.

The forms support broad comparison, but do not establish precise graphic changes or date the earliest uses of 大. The proposed development from “adult” to “big” has no documented dated sequence of intermediate uses.
